subject: Discordant ratings — resolution workflow & confidential HR path
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Calibration prep: flagged discordant ratings + agenda

Team —

Quick note: while prepping the Q3 calibration packet I flagged three rating pairs across Eng + Platform where the median differs by more than two bands (see attached Q3_calibration_team_summary.xlsx). I want us to treat one of these as a confidential adjudication (sensitive manager comments involved).

Proposed prep and agenda:
- Please review the attached summary and the two pages of manager_notes_redacted.pdf before Monday.
- Each manager should add a one-paragraph justification for any rating they want to keep (inline comments in the doc).
- We’ll meet Tuesday 8/17 at 10:30am PT for 45 minutes to review the outliers and decide next steps (canary adjustment, appeal, or HR referral).

I’m copying Mina for HR process guidance. If you think any item is a formal escalation (possible PIP implications), mark it in the sheet and email Mina directly so we can handle confidentiality.

Thanks — keep comments high-level in shared doc; do not forward manager comments outside this thread.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Platform Engineering

Folks —
If this ends up being more than a calibration alignment (i.e., a policy exception or required correction to a rating), we should follow the HR escalation path so the process is auditable. Mina — can you confirm the preference for:

1) Redacted manager notes + consolidated decision logged to People Ops (preferred for sensitive items)
2) Full manager notes in a secure HR folder (if we need to preserve detailed rationale)

I’ve attached a short checklist I use for adjudication calls — happy to run through it in the meeting.

-Michael
Senior Engineering Manager
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Calibration prep: flagged discordant ratings + agenda

Thanks for the heads-up. For clarity and auditability, HR prefers option (1) as the default for manager-led calibrations with sensitive commentary. Process I recommend:

- Managers provide a one-paragraph rationale in the shared doc (redacted of PII or sensitive performance examples).
- People Ops will archive a redacted copy of the packet to the HR folder and maintain a sealed folder with full manager notes if legal/appeal triggers occur.
- If a rating could materially affect comp or promotion, mark that row with "HR-Escalate" and don’t circulate the full comment thread beyond the People Ops team.

I’ll create the sealed HR folder and share a DocuSign consensus form for managers to sign after the calibration call (link below). Please do not include employee names in email replies; refer to IDs or roles in inline comments when needed.

Link: https://app.docusign.com/console/sign/ABC123-calibration-consensus
Drive (redacted): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy_calibration_notes_shared

I’ll also coordinate with PeopleOps Advisory to attach the historical calibration export.

—Mina
Senior People Partner, People Operations
Redwood Inference

—Sean
